next_step: Closed-lost follow-up note + handoff docs to partner team
notes:
Quick CRM snapshot:
- Background: mid-size fintech focused on mortgage securitization analytics. Heavy PII, strict residency for a subset of datasets.
- Timeline: engaged Aug 2024 via event inbound; discovery in Sept; POC started Nov.
- POC scope: chat assistant for underwriting docs + embeddings for historical docket search. Target: 150ms p50 for short queries, sustained 250 rps for batch embed jobs during off-peak. Cost sensitivity high — expected 30-40% reduction vs hosted.
- Security runbook: requested SSO + audit trails + ability to hold keys in-house. Security required offline security review; wanted deployment in private VPC with optional air-gapped test.
- Competitive motion: Procurement leaned toward self-hosted stack after TCO deep-dive. Internal infra favored vLLM + TGI on dedicated infra with TensorRT-LLM for GPU-optimizations. Cited control over model patching and deterministic latency for SLAs.
- Key meetings: 2024-11-08 POC kickoff (Fireflies ff_2024-11-08_arbvlt_call_79ZJ). 2024-12-12 Security deep-dive with Marco + infra lead. 2025-01-07 demo of Redwood routing + canary rollback (requested by engineering manager).
- POC results: generation quality acceptable; cost estimates with Redwood hosted didn't meet finance threshold once committed throughput and retention policies included. Estimated hosted run-rate 2x preferred. Redwood demo impressed SEs but security insisted on in-house KMS + complete network control.
- Stakeholders: CIO (procurement lead), Head of Infra (favored self-host), ML Lead (wanted Redwood if we could guarantee KV caching policies), Legal (concern: third-party data processing for credit data).
- Why closed-lost: after procurement freeze and an infra re-org, decision made to implement in-house using vLLM + TGI orchestration and TensorRT-LLM kernels. Primary reasons cited: cost predictability, full control of keys/data residency, and internal team preference for owning runtime. No single champion remained to push enterprise procurement with Redwood.
- Follow-ups done: handed off security Q&A doc, provided export of POC metrics and cost model (see /drive/pricing). We offered a Dedicated pricing alternative but finance prioritized capex over opex.
- Recommended internal notes: keep warm — 6mo check for post-deploy issues, offer migration plan for hybrid mode (edge/proxy routing back to Redwood for ephemeral workloads). Potential re-engage if infra costs escalate or model ops burden grows.
- Quick quotes from stakeholders: "we need the keys on-prem, and the numbers just don't justify managed for now" — Head of Infra.
- Action items at close: SE to prepare migration playbook (skeleton), AE to set 6mo reminder, send competitive win/loss note to GTM.
